  • What: Talos insight into Salt Typhoon's tactics against telecommunications providers, followed by Cisco's Resilient Infrastructure initiative: specific software changes across IOS XE, IOS XR, NX-OS, ISE, ASA/FTD, and controllers (Catalyst Center, Meraki Dashboard, Catalyst SD-WAN) (from abstract only).
  • How: TTP analysis of the actual attacks, then portfolio-wide hardening changes and the operational preparation needed before deploying secure-by-default software.
  • Where applicable: The lessons apply to networks of all types, not just SPs. The roadmap portion is Cisco-specific — but it's a preview of breaking-change-style hardening other vendors will be pushed toward.

threat-intelligence network-security

items.title: Benchmarking AIML Infrastructure at Scale: AIML Architectures, AI Workloads and Reproducibility for High Performance Data Centers - BRKDCN-2651
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Rakesh Kumar (Cisco), Ram Gandikota (Cisco)

  • Why: The hardest open problem in AI fabrics is trustworthy, reproducible benchmarking — NCCL collective performance is dominated by network behavior and tuning is opaque. This is one of the few sessions engaging with methodology rather than just results.
  • What: The benchmarking methodologies Cisco used across large-scale cluster engagements: alignment with open standards, reproducibility strategies, application-level KPIs like NCCL collectives, network-tuning challenges, and how packet trimming and UEC-based (Ultra Ethernet Consortium) feature alignment are reshaping Ethernet standards for AIML clusters (from abstract only).
  • How: Case-study-driven methodology work — reducing test drift between benchmark and production, making network behavior a first-class measured variable.
  • Where applicable: AI training/inference clusters; the UEC-alignment content matters to anyone planning Ethernet-based AI fabrics. Lessons come from Cisco cluster engagements, so some method choices will be Cisco-toolchain-specific.

benchmarking ai-networks

items.title: Cisco Nexus 9000 Architecture - BRKDCN-3939
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Faraz Taifehesmatian (Cisco)

  • Why: ASIC architecture and forwarding mechanics of the workhorse DC switching line — exactly the "switching internals" content this PM wants, and the substrate for the VXLAN EVPN and AI-fabric sessions elsewhere in the program.
  • What: An in-depth architecture study of the latest-generation Nexus 9000 modular and top-of-rack switches: ASIC architecture, forwarding mechanics, physical design, and hardware-enabled features (from abstract only).
  • How: Internals-first walkthrough rather than feature marketing — how packets actually move through the silicon and what hardware capabilities the feature set leans on.
  • Where applicable: Nexus 9000-specific, but the forwarding-model detail transfers to anyone evaluating DC switch ASICs generally.

switching silicon data-center-fabric

items.title: Cisco Nexus One: An Architecture for your Cisco Datacenter of Tomorrow - BRKDCN-2602
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Adjacent pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Max Ardica (Cisco)

  • Why: Signals how Cisco plans to reconcile its two competing DC architectures (Nexus VXLAN/EVPN and ACI) — relevant strategic context for anyone operating or evaluating either.
  • What: Nexus One: a new architecture integrating Nexus VXLAN/EVPN fabrics with ACI, with seamless traffic flow between the two and single-pane management built around automation and orchestration (from abstract only).
  • How: Integration layer plus unified management/automation across both architectures.
  • Where applicable: Cisco-shop specific and new/unproven; this is architecture direction, not battle-tested deployment. Treat as a roadmap read on vendor convergence strategy.

data-center-fabric

items.title: Demystifying AI Infrastructure for a Network Engineer - BRKDCN-2971
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Paresh Gupta (Cisco)

  • Why: RDMA/lossless Ethernet is squarely this PM's core territory, and this session packages the current AI-fabric networking stack — RoCE, PFC, DC QCN, collective libraries, Spectrum-X, Ultra Ethernet — in one place. Framed as intro, but the content map is the industry's Ethernet-for-AI state of play.
  • What: How GPUs communicate during distributed AI jobs and how that traffic differs from ordinary DC workloads; covers RoCE, PFC, DC QCN; collective operations via NCCL/RCCL/HCCL; NVIDIA Spectrum-X's problem statement and solution; and where Cisco Nexus, Hyperfabric for AI, and Ultra Ethernet fit (from abstract only).
  • How: Fundamentals-first build-up from GPU communication patterns to lossless-fabric mechanisms and vendor approaches.
  • Where applicable: AI/ML cluster fabric design generally. The Spectrum-X comparison is inevitably vendor-slanted; the RoCE/PFC/QCN and NCCL material is standard. Skip if you already operate RoCE fabrics day-to-day.

ai-networks rdma congestion-control

items.title: Designing Next-Generation DC and WAN Networks for the Neo-Cloud Era with Cisco 8000, SONiC and XR - BRKMSI-1471
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Adjacent pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Krithika Moorthy (Cisco), Jiri Chaloupka (Cisco)

  • Why: The IOS XR (WAN/backbone) + SONiC (DC) split as a deliberate two-NOS operating model is a useful reference pattern, even if presented through Cisco's reference-architecture lens.
  • What: The Neo-Cloud reference architecture: IOS XR for backbone roles, SONiC for data center functions, unified operations across DC and WAN; high-performance interconnect design, multi-vendor interoperability, capacity planning, redundancy, and traffic optimization, illustrated with real-world use cases (from abstract only).
  • How: Role-based OS assignment across domains with an operations layer aimed at consistency between them.
  • Where applicable: Cisco reference architecture; the pattern (split NOS by domain, unified ops) generalizes, but specifics are Cisco 8000-family-bound.

data-center-fabric open-source

items.title: Designing Zero Trust Data Center Segmentation Architecture - BRKDCN-2930
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Cesar Obediente (Cisco), Brenden Buresh (Cisco)

  • Why: A structured progression from traditional DC firewalling to layered zero-trust segmentation, and it notably brings DPU/SmartSwitch and host-based (Isovalent/Cilium-lineage) enforcement into the same policy model as the fabric — the network/host security convergence this PM tracks.
  • What: How to build DC segmentation in layers on a Nexus 9K VXLAN EVPN baseline: macro-segmentation with VRFs, micro-segmentation with VXLAN GPO (L4 stateless), then adding DPU SmartSwitch and Isovalent host-based agents for L4 stateful controls, culminating in a hybrid mesh firewall concept with one central security controller authoring policy across network, host, and appliance enforcement points (from abstract only).
  • How: Incremental architecture: each layer adds enforcement capability without discarding the previous; single policy authority distributed to multiple enforcement points.
  • Where applicable: Nexus 9K + Cisco DPU/Isovalent stack for the full vision, but the macro/micro-segmentation layering pattern is general. The "hybrid mesh firewall" portion is Cisco's emerging architecture — treat as direction-setting rather than proven production pattern.

zero-trust data-center-fabric network-security

items.title: Enterprise-Ready Agentic Workflows: Hardening MCP with Policy-as-Code - DEVNET-2685
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Lori Jakab (Cisco)

  • Why: MCP is spreading into network automation exactly where this PM operates, and its security model is genuinely immature. Applying OPA/Rego to JSON-RPC MCP traffic is a concrete, standards-agnostic pattern — policy-as-Code spanning agents and traditional automation is a real near-term need.
  • What: Why MCP's current authentication mechanisms fall short of enterprise requirements, and how to harden MCP servers with Policy-as-Code: OPA and Rego applied to JSON-RPC messages between MCP clients and servers, unifying access control across agentic workflows and existing API/script-based automation (from abstract only).
  • How: Extend policy enforcement from traditional API payloads to MCP JSON-RPC messages via OPA, with demonstrations including real-world Cisco deployment scenarios.
  • Where applicable: General technique (OPA/Rego are open source; MCP is an open protocol), not locked to Cisco infrastructure — though demos are Cisco-centric. Requires comfort with automation tooling.

authorization automation

items.title: Everything You Ever Wanted to Know about Power in Routers and Switches (and Quite a Bit More) - PSOGRN-2161
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

LJ Wobker (Cisco), Lane Wigley (Cisco)

  • Why: Power and thermal are now first-order constraints in DC design — with AI racks pushing 150-250 kW, understanding what actually moves power consumption in network gear (and what doesn't) is core systems knowledge, not facilities trivia.
  • What: A systematic treatment of power in network equipment: provisioning vs. typical vs. peak; per-component breakdowns; effects of traffic and temperature; PSU efficiency; optics power; conversion loss; redundancy models; thermals in high-power systems; and which off-peak "power saving" measures actually help — supported by system-test examples (from abstract only).
  • How: Measurement-driven: system testing examples are used to ground claims about how load, temperature, and configuration change real draw.
  • Where applicable: General across router/switch platforms; concrete numbers will be Cisco-specific but the methodology (typical vs. worst-case provisioning, optics power accounting) is broadly applicable.

power switching

items.title: Hijacking Trust: Weaponizing Stolen Cookies and Tokens - BRKSEC-2132
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Stefan Duernberger (Cisco)

  • Why: Session-token theft via adversary-in-the-middle proxies is now the dominant bypass of password- and MFA-based authentication. For an identity-focused PM, the defensive side here — device-bound credentials and shared signals — is the current frontier.
  • What: Real-world session hijacking techniques using tools like Evilginx and EvilnoVNC to steal authentication cookies, then the defensive stack: OAuth 2.0/OIDC mechanics, Google's Device-Bound Session Credentials (DBSC), Cisco Duo Passport, and the Shared Signals and Events framework for continuous authentication trust (from abstract only).
  • How: Offense-then-defense: demonstrate the cookie-theft flow, then show how device-bound session credentials and shared-signals eventing close it.
  • Where applicable: Broadly applicable to web authentication generally; DBSC is browser-dependent (Chromium lineage) and Duo Passport is Cisco product, but the protocol analysis is vendor-neutral.

authentication identity threat-intelligence

items.title: How the World's Largest Backbone Provider is Leveraging the AI Opportunity - CSSAI-1596
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Abeel Choudry (Cisco), Dariusz Solowiej Solowiej (Arelion)

  • Why: Arelion carries ~70% of global internet routes — backbone-scale evidence of what converged IP/optical architecture does at the extreme end of WAN. Treat the headline percentages with appropriate skepticism; the scale detail is the value.
  • What: How Arelion claims to have achieved 66% CapEx and 95% OpEx reduction while repositioning for AI-driven traffic, via Routed Optical Networking with coherent optics, Silicon One-based Cisco 8000 routers, and automated assurance (from abstract only).
  • How: Network convergence collapsing transport layers, plus automation/analytics for service assurance and moves toward self-healing networks and self-service capabilities.
  • Where applicable: Arelion-specific — a single global backbone operator with twice its nearest competitor's capacity. The percentages are vendor-co-presented and unaudited; the architectural direction (coherent pluggables in routed ports, heavy automation) is where the whole industry is heading. Watch for whether they give real before/after operational detail.

ai-networks interconnection optics

items.title: How to Network LLMs. Splitting Large Language Models Running on GPUs Across a Network - BRKOPS-2931
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Wildcard pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Dave Zacks (Cisco), Patrick leMaistre (Cisco)

  • Why: Not a core interest for this PM, but inverts the usual AI-fabric question: instead of "what network does training need," it asks "what the network must look like to host disaggregated inference/models across hosts" — on-prem, with private local datasets. A different lens on why DC fabric design is changing.
  • What: How LLMs that don't fit in one GPU or one server are split across multiple hosts and linked by the network, focusing on what a properly designed network must provide for distributed, on-premises AI model hosting (from abstract only).
  • How: Deep-dive walkthrough (by two veteran Cisco Live speakers) of model partitioning across systems and the network requirements that result.
  • Where applicable: On-prem AI model hosting scenarios; likely conceptual rather than benchmarked, and inevitably Cisco-portfolio-flavored. The abstraction transfers to any fabric supporting split models.

ai-networks gpu-clusters

items.title: Introduction to eBPF - BRKSEC-2169
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Adjacent pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Liz Rice (Cisco)

  • Why: Liz Rice is the most credible popularizer of eBPF, and her presence on the Cisco roster (via Isovalent) reflects how deeply eBPF is being absorbed into Cisco's security and networking strategy. For a PM already fluent in eBPF/Cilium, the technology content will be familiar — the signal is the messenger and venue.
  • What: An in-depth introduction to eBPF: origins, rewards, challenges, with live demos of what eBPF is and how it enables high-performance security, networking, and observability capabilities (from abstract only).
  • How: Live demonstration-driven explanation of eBPF's mechanics and why it has been called "superpowers for Linux."
  • Where applicable: Foundational and vendor-neutral in content. Skip if you already work with eBPF daily; useful for onboarding colleagues or calibrating how a major vendor is positioning the technology.

ebpf linux-networking

items.title: Lessons Navigating from Proof of Concept to Production with IP/Optical Convergence: How DT is Evolving their Transport Network with Cisco Routed Optical Networking - CSSENS-2717
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Nils Warnke (Deutsche Telekom), Silke Bauten (Cisco)

  • Why: This is the standout end-user talk of the set: an operator's lead architect explaining how IP/optical convergence actually got done — the organizational and qualification friction, not the slideware. DT projects over 85% energy savings from collapsing standalone optical gear into coherent pluggables on routed ports, a number worth pressure-testing in the Q&A.
  • What: DT's Horizontal Digital Architecture network evolution: moving from a technology vision to production, covering four readiness areas — hardware qualification of pluggables across Cisco and third-party host platforms, process automation to cut service lead time, cross-domain operations/assurance (alarm correlation), and field/capacity readiness for rollout (from abstract only).
  • How: Real deployment narrative: integrating roles and responsibilities across IP and optical teams, and building qualification, automation, and assurance workflows around pluggable-based transport.
  • Where applicable: DT-specific production setup, but the lessons (multi-vendor host qualification, org merging of IP and optical teams) generalize to any carrier or large DC operator pursuing convergence. Numbers are projections, not necessarily measured results.

optics interconnection

items.title: Life of a Packet in Kubernetes: A Network Engineer's Guide - BRKCLD-3734
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Nico Vibert (Cisco)

  • Why: This hits the PM's cloud-native interests almost exactly: Cilium as dataplane, Gateway API, BGP, egress, IPsec, DSR, BIG TCP, topology-aware routing — mapped onto a full packet journey rather than feature-by-feature.
  • What: An advanced, demo-driven trace of a packet through a Kubernetes cluster: VXLAN/Geneve overlays, Gateway API, Egress Gateway, BGP routing, IPsec encryption, DSR, multi-cluster Cluster Mesh, plus performance features (BIG TCP, topology-aware traffic engineering) and troubleshooting with Hubble, Cilium CLI, and Wireshark (from abstract only).
  • How: Packet-walk structure — follow real traffic through encapsulation, routing, policy, and encryption layers, correlating observed behavior with Kubernetes constructs.
  • Where applicable: Cilium/Isovalent-specific dataplane (that's the point — it's the de facto eBPF dataplane), but the overlay/routing/egress mechanics transfer to most CNI implementations. Assumes solid IP and Kubernetes grounding.

kubernetes ebpf cni

items.title: Preparation Guide to Emergency Comms and Networking using Amateur Radios (HAM) - BRKGEN-1012
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Wildcard pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Jimmy Alignay (Cisco)

  • Why: Genuinely off-pattern for a vendor conference: packet radio's role in the origins of IP networking (ALOHAnet → ARPANET lineage), plus practical emergency-comms deployments from hurricanes Helene and Milton 2024. A reminder of what "carrier-free" networking looks like and why foundational comms matter in disaster ops.
  • What: The history of packet switching from ALOHAnet through amateur packet radio to modern IP, real-world emergency communications deployments supporting first responders and network operations after the 2024 hurricanes, and how modern amateur radio integrates Layer 2/Layer 3 networking with Cisco gear and Starlink (from abstract only).
  • How: Historical narrative plus tactical deployment case studies and practical guidance for getting started.
  • Where applicable: Emergency-preparedness and remote-site contexts; the historical networking content (ALOHAnet's influence on Ethernet's CSMA lineage) is a genuinely interesting wildcard for anyone who cares about where the technology came from.

troubleshooting spectrum

items.title: Preparing for AI Workloads: Options for Integrated Rack Power and Cooling Systems - BRKCOM-2530
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Wildcard pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Christopher Liljenstolpe (Cisco), Fabio Gori (Cisco)

  • Why: Per-rack power planning jumping from 16-30 kW to 150-250+ kW in two years is the physical constraint that will reshape DC topology, cabling, and even optics choices — this is adjacent to the PM's physical-DC world but its consequences land squarely in it.
  • What: The impact of rack power and thermal density choices on AI-ready facilities, how AI can optimize cooling energy and workload distribution across servers, and how to select cooling systems that prioritize energy efficiency without compromising performance (from abstract only).
  • How: Options analysis across integrated rack power/cooling approaches, with AI-assisted optimization of cooling and workload placement.
  • Where applicable: New AI build-outs and retrofits; the 150-250+ kW/rack figures are hyperscale/AI-cluster-specific. Liljenstolpe's DC background suggests this will be more grounded than a facilities-vendor pitch.

power data-center-fabric

items.title: Redefining Netflix BGP Architecture with IOS-XRv 9000 Route-Reflector Appliance - CSSENS-2442
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Frederic Cuiller (Cisco), Elise VENNEGUES (Netflix)

  • Why: A joint operator/vendor case study on BGP route-reflector architecture at global scale — BGP internals plus the messy realities of validation and migration, told by the operator themselves.
  • What: How Netflix and Cisco evolved Netflix's BGP architecture around the IOS XRv9000 on a UCS M7 appliance, developed and refined against Netflix's requirements: motivations, design, validation, deployment, and migration strategy with lessons learned (from abstract only).
  • How: Design-and-migrate narrative: technical challenges, collaborative development, validation and best practices for a seamless transition from the previous route-reflector setup.
  • Where applicable: Netflix-specific in scale and requirements, but the route-reflector appliance pattern and migration methodology generalize to any large SP or edge network. Expect concrete only if the speakers go deep on validation data.

bgp troubleshooting

items.title: Rethinking Identity, Policy, and Access Control (IPAC) for Agentic AI - BRKETI-2623
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Marcelo Yannuzzi (Cisco)

  • Why: Agentic identity is where the PM's identity work is heading, and this is one of the first vendor architectures that names the actual problem: current IAM scopes, scopes authorization around humans and static service accounts, not autonomous NL-driven entities acting at machine speed.
  • What: The technology gaps in today's IAM for agentic AI, and a proposed IPAC architecture covering: dynamic trust establishment among users, agents, and MCP servers (Just-In-Time identification, Multi-Factor Verification across domains), policy that defines what autonomous entities may do without a human in the loop, and granular authorization for entities communicating in natural language — with a demo and pointers to Cisco's open-source efforts (from abstract only).
  • How: Architecture-plus-demo: identify the gaps (static identity, human-in-loop assumptions), then layer JIT identification and policy enforcement over agent/MCP interactions.
  • Where applicable: Early-stage/forward-looking — this is where the field is going rather than where it is. Note the SPIFFE/SPIRE-shaped hole: workload-identity primitives would be the natural substrate, worth probing in Q&A. Cisco "innovations and open source efforts" means expect some product framing.

identity authorization

items.title: The New, QUIC Based Encrypted Protocol Stack Taking over the Internet and How to Deal with It - BRKSPM-2024
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Andreas Enotiadis (Cisco), Bart Van de Velde (Cisco)

  • Why: QUIC + HTTP/3 + DoH + ECH is dismantling the visibility and traffic-management assumptions most network and security infrastructure was built on. The abstract cites QUIC at ~50% of total traffic, doubling every 18 months — a structural shift, not an SP niche topic.
  • What: How the QUIC-based encrypted stack is constructed and evolving, its behavior in terms of visibility and flow control, its impact on infrastructure elements, and the techniques providers can use to keep pace — traffic visibility, QoE monitoring/management, and efficient use of 5G spectrum (from abstract only).
  • How: Protocol-level decomposition: TLS 1.3 encryption removing application visibility, congestion management moving into the application, applications disintermediating the network.
  • Where applicable: Framed for service providers, but the visibility loss applies to any enterprise DC or security team doing traffic inspection, QoS, or telemetry on the wire.

http tls encryption

items.title: VXLAN EVPN: A Deep Dive into Packet Forwarding - BRKDCN-3966
items.text:
Cisco Live Europe 2026 (Amsterdam) digest Program Core pick Amsterdam · 9–13 February 2026

Abstract

Lukas Krattiger (Cisco)

  • Why: EVPN is the dominant DC overlay control plane and datapath-debugging knowledge is where most operational pain lives. This is a datapath-internals talk, not an EVPN primer.
  • What: A packet-by-packet walkthrough of VXLAN EVPN forwarding — routing, bridging, and multi-destination handling from ingress VTEP through to egress VTEP and beyond (from abstract only).
  • How: "Day in the life of a packet" structure following a concrete frame through the overlay.
  • Where applicable: Any VXLAN EVPN fabric (Nexus 9K baseline is Cisco's, but the mechanics are standard). Assumes working EVPN knowledge.

bgp data-center-fabric

items.title: 400G, 800G, and Terabit Pluggable Optics: What You Need to Know - BRKOPT-2699
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Mark Nowell (Cisco), Errol Roberts (Cisco)

  • Why: The optics roadmap is now the binding constraint on DC fabric design — power, reach, and breakout options determine what topologies are even buildable. Nowell is a long-standing IEEE 802.3 optics contributor, which makes this a standards-insider survey rather than a datasheet read.
  • What: A survey of current 400G pluggable optics and their applications, next-generation 800G/1.6T form factors including breakout use cases, the status of 800 Gb/s and 1.6 Tb/s Ethernet standardization, and co-packaged optics (integrating optical interfaces into switch ASICs), framed by industry dynamics and AI-driven demand (from abstract only).
  • How: Technology survey across form factors, IEEE standardization tracks, and co-packaging directions, covering both coherent and noncoherent optics.
  • Where applicable: Broadly applicable to anyone specifying optical interconnect for DC or DCI — the standards and form-factor content is vendor-neutral even though the speaker is Cisco. Assumes working deployment knowledge of optical modules.

items.title: Advancements and Applications of Coherent Pluggable Technology in High Bandwidth Transport Networks - BRKOPT-2556
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Anuj Malik (Cisco)

  • Why: Coherent pluggables are collapsing the boundary between the IP and optical layers — directly relevant to DC/WAN interconnect, where the same pluggable now serves router ports and line systems.
  • What: The technical underpinnings of coherent pluggables — tunable lasers, high-speed ADC/DACs, DSP algorithms — plus performance comparisons (data rates, reach, power consumption) against traditional coherent solutions, real-world deployment scenarios, and the trend toward IP/optical convergence (from abstract only).
  • How: Coherent DSP packaged into pluggable transceiver form factors, compared against embedded coherent line systems on rate/reach/power metrics.
  • Where applicable: High-bandwidth transport and DCI. Vendor talk, so expect the case studies to favor Cisco outcomes, but the component physics and metric trade-offs are general.

items.title: An Introduction to Quantum Mechanics, Computing, and Networking - BRKETI-1401
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Wildcard pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Tim Szigeti (Cisco)

  • Why: Cisco is making a serious R&D bet on quantum networking, and this is the clearest signal in the program of where the long-horizon network and security landscape may move (distributed quantum computing, entanglement-based secure communications, clock sync).
  • What: An introduction to quantum mechanics focused on qubits and their special properties — superposition, entanglement, no-cloning, including mathematical proofs — an overview of quantum computing's impact on network communications and security, and the building blocks, opportunities, and challenges of quantum networks, plus Cisco's current work (from abstract only).
  • How: Tutorial format; foundational science first, then networking implications.
  • Where applicable: Nothing here is deployable today — it is forward-looking R&D context, useful for spotting the trajectory rather than near-term engineering.

items.title: Are You Prepared for the Next Typhoon? - BRKSEC-2499
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Paul Giralt (Cisco), Steve Nowell (Cisco)

  • Why: Salt Typhoon is the defining nation-state compromise of network infrastructure in this era, and this session combines Talos threat insight with concrete hardening guidance plus Cisco's "secure by default" roadmap — with an explicit feedback opportunity on that roadmap.
  • What: The nature of the 2024 Salt Typhoon intrusions across multi-vendor infrastructure at major telecoms as understood by Talos, specific hardening steps available today, and planned future "secure by default" enhancements to network infrastructure (from abstract only).
  • How: Attack-surface analysis followed by hardening best practices and defensive-design changes.
  • Where applicable: Broadly applicable to network infrastructure security; telecom operators are the most-affected vertical, but the hardening lessons apply to any operator of carrier or enterprise network gear.

items.title: Cisco Nexus 9000 Architecture - BRKDCN-3939
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Faraz Taifehesmatian (Cisco)

  • Why: Switching silicon and forwarding internals are squarely in the PM's core interest; this is the deep-dive on the ASIC generation that underpins the AI-fabric sessions above.
  • What: An in-depth architecture study of the latest Nexus 9000 modular and top-of-rack switches: ASIC architecture, forwarding mechanics, physical design elements, and the hardware-enabled features that deliver DC network services (from abstract only).
  • How: Architecture walkthrough from silicon to system.
  • Where applicable: Cisco-specific silicon, but the trade-offs discussed (buffering, forwarding pipeline, physical design) are transferable to evaluating any modern DC switch ASIC.

items.title: Connecting Your Data to LLMs: Identity, Functions and Agents are all you Need - BRKETI-2411
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Adjacent pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Guillaume De Saint Marc (Cisco)

  • Why: Agentic identity is one of the PM's explicit interests and almost absent from vendor programs — this is the closest hit: per-request authorization deciding which data an agent may fetch and serve.
  • What: Architectures and tools for connecting enterprise data (including on-prem) to LLMs without data migration, including real-time prompt inspection to identify the data required by a request, determine whether the user has rightful access, and serve only authorized data (from abstract only).
  • How: Prompt-time authorization — mapping an incoming prompt to data requirements and checking entitlements before data is served to the model.
  • Where applicable: Enterprise GenAI deployments; Cisco brings product positioning, but the underlying pattern — entitlement-aware data serving for agent requests — is broadly relevant to anyone designing agentic identity.

items.title: Deep Dive into Cisco's Use of QUIC, MASQUE and OS Native Capabilities to Deliver Frictionless Zero Trust Access - BRKSEC-3027
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Vinny Parla (Cisco)

  • Why: Shows where identity and transport converge: MASQUE/QUIC-based access proxied through OS-native clients from Apple, Google, and Samsung, with WebAuthn and passkeys in the loop — a credible picture of how frictionless ZTNA gets to Wi-Fi-level ubiquity.
  • What: How industry-standard protocols (MASQUE, QUIC, WebAuthn, passkeys, private 5G) can deliver Zero Trust Access with minimal user/admin friction; how native OS clients from Apple and Samsung and the Cisco Zero Trust Access module in Cisco Secure Client leverage MASQUE and QUIC for a seamless experience (from abstract only).
  • How: MASQUE-style proxying over QUIC tunnels integrated with OS-native network clients and passkey-based user identity.
  • Where applicable: Enterprise and consumer device access; heavily ecosystem-dependent (collaboration with Apple, Google, Samsung), so the OS-client pieces are platform-specific while the protocol layer is standard.

items.title: Deployment of Micro-Segmentation in Cisco NX-OS VXLAN EVPN Fabrics with VXLAN Group Policy Option (GPO) - BRKDCN-2633
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Max Ardica (Cisco)

  • Why: East-west segmentation enforced in the fabric itself — the intersection of the PM's network security and DC overlay interests — and grounded in an IETF draft rather than a purely proprietary mechanism.
  • What: Micro-segmentation using security groups and security group ACLs in NX-OS VXLAN EVPN fabrics via VXLAN Group Policy Option (IETF draft-smith-vxlan-group-policy-05), covering the control- and data-plane components of the implementation and common use cases including service-chaining simplification (from abstract only).
  • How: Group policy conveyed in the VXLAN header so per-application policy follows the workload anywhere in the fabric, replacing perimeter-centric inspection.
  • Where applicable: NX-OS EVPN fabrics; the mechanism follows an IETF draft so the concept is portable, but the described implementation is Cisco-specific.

items.title: Ethernet Evolution and Challenges in the world of AI - BRKNWT-2504
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Kapil Mehta (Cisco)

  • Why: This is the lossless-fabric problem the PM works on daily — RDMA and elephant flows breaking Ethernet's assumptions in AI back-end networks — plus a read on where Ultra Ethernet Consortium standardization is actually heading.
  • What: Ethernet's evolution history, its current failure modes under AI switching workloads (RDMA, elephant packet flows), Cisco's solutions, and the innovations being standardized by the Ultra Ethernet Consortium (from abstract only).
  • How: Survey of the mechanisms being applied to congestion and losslessness at AI scale, positioned against UEC's standardization work items.
  • Where applicable: AI back-end networks generally; the problem framing is industry-wide, but the "solutions" portion will be Cisco-flavored.

items.title: EVPN Fabric in the Real World: Securing Critical Infrastructure in Finance and Aviation - BRKENS-2655
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Adjacent pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Daniel Cantor (Fiserv), Ekta Ghosh (Adani Airports Holding Limited), Rahul Kachalia (Cisco)

  • Why: Two real end users (Fiserv, Adani Airports) discussing EVPN-fabric modernization under regulatory pressure. Worth a look for the case-study value, but the abstract is executive-framed ("high-impact executive session") and offers no metrics, failure discussion, or technical depth — approach with skepticism.
  • What: How Fiserv and Adani Airports used Catalyst networking and EVPN fabric as the foundation for automated, always-on infrastructure, with claimed reductions in downtime and improved security posture (from abstract only — no numbers in the abstract; verify specifics in the recording).
  • How: Executive discussion/Q&A format per the abstract.
  • Where applicable: Regulated enterprise environments (financial services, aviation/airports); campus and DC-edge scale rather than hyperscale.

items.title: Groq: An AI Success Story - Deploying High-Performance, and Low-Latency AI Networks Using Cisco Nexus 9000 - CSSDCN-2005
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Swetha Velamuri (Cisco), Cameron Ferdinands (Groq)

  • Why: A real customer (Groq) describing inference-network design — inference traffic has different characteristics from training (latency-critical, bursty, iterative) and public detail on inference fabrics is scarce.
  • What: How Groq uses Nexus 9000/NX-OS to achieve scalability, bandwidth, low latency, and congestion management for AI inference, plus how Cisco optics choices reduce cost and energy (from abstract only — the abstract makes performance and cost claims without numbers; treat specifics as unverified until seen in the recording).
  • How: Groq's software-first hardware approach paired with Nexus congestion management and optics innovations.
  • Where applicable: Groq-specific inference deployments; success-story framing with a Cisco co-speaker, so expect a product-friendly narrative rather than a post-mortem.

items.title: How Cisco build AI readiness IP Backbone with 8000 Series - BRKMSI-3000
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Rob Piasecki (Cisco), Ruben Lopes da Fonte (Cisco)

  • Why: Rare config-level treatment of lossless fabric mechanics — RoCEv2, PFC, ECN — including CLI verification, which is exactly the lossless-fabric internals the PM wants, not just architecture slideware.
  • What: How Cisco builds AI infrastructure for webscalers: the requirements, the RoCEv2/PFC/ECN technology, detailed IOS-XR configuration, CLI verification that PFC and ECN are working, and design guidance (from abstract only — note the abstract itself is typo-laden, suggesting a hands-on rather than polished session).
  • How: Step-by-step IOS-XR configuration of PFC and ECN with CLI validation, wrapped in design recommendations for AI-ready IP backbones.
  • Where applicable: Platform-specific to Cisco 8000-series/IOS-XR, but the design principles (ECN threshold tuning, PFC behavior verification, lossless design patterns) transfer to any RoCEv2 fabric.

items.title: Impact of AI Traffic in Transport Networks - BRKSPG-1180
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Adjacent pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Virginia Teixeira (Cisco)

  • Why: Near-core for anyone responsible for DC/WAN interconnect: AI traffic patterns (RAG, grounding, agents, edge distribution) change DCI and WAN dimensioning assumptions in ways transport teams haven't absorbed yet.
  • What: An analysis of AI traffic characteristics across a set of AI use cases and their impact on WAN and DCI design requirements (from abstract only).
  • How: Traffic-pattern characterization mapped onto transport network design levers.
  • Where applicable: Service-provider and large-enterprise transport. The speaker's own framing is honest that AI deployment models are still settling, so expect early directional analysis rather than settled engineering rules.

items.title: Innovative Authentication: Beyond Passwords - BRKSEC-2584
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Stefan Duernberger (Cisco)

  • Why: Directly the identity stack the PM tracks — passkeys, OAuth 2.0/OIDC — plus two genuinely emerging items (Google's Device-Bound Session Credentials and Shared Signals and Events) that sit beyond the basics.
  • What: The role and implementation of passkeys, OAuth 2.0 and OIDC for cross-platform authentication, Google DBSC, Cisco Duo Passport, and an overview of Shared Signals and Events — all framed within a Zero Trust architecture (from abstract only).
  • How: Protocol survey connecting credential technology (passkeys/WebAuthn) to authorization frameworks (OAuth/OIDC) to session-integrity (DBSC) and continuous-signal (SSSE) mechanisms.
  • Where applicable: General web and enterprise authentication; the Duo Passport portion is Cisco product content, but the protocol material is standards-based and general.

items.title: Multi-Tier Fabrics: Network Designs for the Modern Data Center - BRKDCN-2999
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Adjacent pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Marina Ferreira (Cisco)

  • Why: The back half of this session is genuinely relevant physical-DC content — super-spine and hyperscale plane designs, where 400G/800G is cost-effective, fixed vs. modular trade-offs, and routed fabrics for cloud-native applications. The front half is Clos 101, which the PM doesn't need; hence adjacent rather than core.
  • What: Fat-tree, Clos, and leaf/spine foundations extended to super-spine and hyperscale plane designs, cost-effective use of 400G/800G, fixed-vs-modular switch decisions, and a review of self-organized routed fabrics for cloud-native applications (from abstract only).
  • How: Design-pattern survey with cost/scale reasoning.
  • Where applicable: General data center design, vendor-neutral in principle; the routed-fabric segment connects to the same IP-underlay-for-cloud trend the PM sees in Kubernetes environments.

items.title: Optimizing AI-Ready WAN Infrastructure with Microsoft and Cisco - CSSENT-2100
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Sarav Subramanian (Microsoft), Ruben Lopes da Fonte (Cisco), Gaisin Rustam (Microsoft)

  • Why: An end-user case study from Microsoft on deploying RDMA in the Azure WAN — extending lossless-network practice beyond the DC into the WAN, which few operators talk about publicly.
  • What: How AI-ready infrastructure is being built in the Azure WAN using RDMA for high throughput, low latency, and lossless transfer with minimal CPU load, and the congestion-management strategies (Priority Flow Control, ECN) used to handle oversubscription and microbursts (from abstract only).
  • How: RDMA across WAN infrastructure with PFC/ECN congestion control for microburst and oversubscription scenarios.
  • Where applicable: Microsoft Azure WAN-specific setup. Joint vendor-customer session, so expect some marketing gloss, but the scenario — lossless behavior at WAN scale — is unusually candid territory for Microsoft to discuss.

items.title: Packet Buddy - Chatting with your PCAPs, via the Cloud or Locally on Your Own Machine! - AIHUB-2000
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Wildcard pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Dave Zacks (Cisco), Prapanch Ramamoorthy (Cisco)

  • Why: LLM-assisted packet analysis is a genuinely new tool category, and the PM lives in PCAPs — this is the kind of thing worth knowing exists before it lands in a commercial product.
  • What: An open-source solution ("PACKET BUDDY") that lets you chat with your own Wireshark captures via a choice of LLMs — asking what traffic is present, what errors it sees, and getting help understanding packets and flows — deployable via cloud or locally on your own machine (from abstract only).
  • How: PCAP ingestion fed to an LLM with conversational querying; the local deployment option is the privacy-relevant detail.
  • Where applicable: Any environment; open source, with the obvious caveat that feeding captures to cloud LLMs has data-exposure implications — the local mode matters.

items.title: Packets in Space: Networking for the Final Frontier - CISCOU-1057
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Wildcard pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Lexie Cooper (Blue Origin), Eric Peterson (Blue Origin), Patrick Garggan (Cisco)

  • Why: Designing networks where failure is not an option and latency requirements are extreme forces first-principles thinking that is useful calibration for anyone building "critical" terrestrial infrastructure.
  • What: A moderated Q&A with Blue Origin "rocket network engineers" on designing mission-critical networks for rockets and spacecraft — real-time telemetry, low-latency requirements, and extreme environmental conditions (from abstract only — note the program abstract is truncated mid-sentence, so the full scope of the session is unclear from the text alone).
  • How: Q&A format rather than a prepared technical talk.
  • Where applicable: Aerospace-specific, but the deterministic, failure-intolerant design lessons generalize to any network with hard availability and timing requirements.

items.title: Security superpowers with eBPF and Tetragon - BRKSEC-2167
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Liz Rice (Cisco)

  • Why: Liz Rice is one of the leading voices in eBPF/Cilium, and Tetragon is the open-source enforcement engine underneath Cisco's Hypershield — this session reveals where a major vendor's security stack is actually being built, from a contributor rather than a marketer.
  • What: A deep dive into Tetragon: YAML tracing policies mapped to eBPF programs attached to a variety of event types, multi-program "following" of a series of events to pinpoint likely-malicious behavior, and in-kernel event aggregation/filtering to minimize observability overhead (from abstract only).
  • How: eBPF programs attached at kernel event points; policy-based correlation across event sequences; in-kernel aggregation and filtering to keep overhead low.
  • Where applicable: Linux hosts and Kubernetes broadly — Tetragon is open source and vendor-neutral in applicability, while also being the substrate for Cisco's commercial Hypershield.

items.title: SONiC Architecture and Deployment Deep Dive - BRKMSI-2004
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Jiri Chaloupka (Cisco)

  • Why: SONiC is where open-source NOS momentum actually is, and a Cisco deep dive covering SONiC on their own Silicon One dataplane is a strong signal about where the disaggregation story is heading — including AI back-end networks as a deployment driver.
  • What: Part one covers SONiC's OS architecture in detail with examples of SONiC running on Cisco Silicon One NPU/data plane; part two covers deployment examples and when SONiC should be considered, including AI frontend and back-end networks (from abstract only).
  • How: Architecture decomposition of SONiC's componentized design, followed by deployment-decision guidance.
  • Where applicable: SONiC on Cisco hardware specifically, but the architecture content and the "when to choose SONiC" framing apply to any disaggregated-NOS evaluation.

items.title: The Swiss Army Knife of Cloud Native Networking - BRKCLD-1012
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Raymond De Jong (Cisco)

  • Why: Hits the PM's Cilium/BGP/IPAM interests directly — BGP from Cilium and LB IPAM for multi-tenant pools are the operational pieces most teams hit in production.
  • What: Cilium's advanced features — BGP, load balancing, LB IPAM, and network policies — for multi-cloud and multi-tenancy networking, including routing/connectivity between Kubernetes clusters and external networks, BGP setup across different topologies, and multi-tenant routing with multiple IP pools for LoadBalancer IP assignment (from abstract only).
  • How: eBPF datapath (Cilium) with a BGP control plane for external reachability, and LB IPAM pools giving platform engineers per-tenant LB IP allocation.
  • Where applicable: General Cilium/Kubernetes environments; mechanisms are open source even though the speaker is Cisco.

items.title: VXLAN EVPN: A Deep Dive into Packet Forwarding - BRKDCN-3966
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2025 (San Diego) digest Program Core pick San Diego · 8–12 June 2025

Abstract

Lukas Krattiger (Cisco)

  • Why: "A day in the life of a packet" is exactly the datapath-internals treatment the PM values — most EVPN content covers control plane; this follows the data plane.
  • What: How routing and bridging actually happen across a VXLAN EVPN fabric — what occurs from the ingress VTEP through to the egress VTEP and beyond, including how multi-destination traffic is handled (from abstract only).
  • How: Step-by-step packet walk through the overlay, ingress to egress.
  • Where applicable: The mechanics are general to VXLAN EVPN regardless of vendor; examples will be NX-OS-based.

items.title: 400G, 800G, and Terabit Pluggable Optics: What You Need to Know - BRKOPT-2699
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Mark Nowell (Cisco), Errol Roberts (Cisco)

  • Why: Optics is a listed core interest, and this is the standards-and-roadmap session covering the full 400G→1.6T transition.
  • What: Current 400G pluggable technologies and applications, next-gen form factors for 800G and 1.6T (including breakout use cases), the new 800Gb/s and 1.6Tb/s Ethernet standardization work, and optical co-packaging developments for integrating optics into ASICs (from abstract only).
  • How: Covers both coherent and non-coherent optics, what's driving each development, and the system/network implications of adopting them.
  • Where applicable: Broadly applicable industry roadmap rather than a Cisco product pitch (Mark Nowell is a long-time IEEE 802.3 participant); co-packaging and LPO/LRO implications matter to any high-density DC design.

optics ethernet

items.title: A Quantum Leap in Networking: Cisco's Blueprint for Tomorrow's Infrastructure - CENETI-1281
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Wildcard pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Ramana Kompella (Cisco)

  • Why: Not a fit for daily work, but a credible roadmap signal: Cisco is committing to quantum networking on a ~5-year horizon, with named artifacts and partners.
  • What: Cisco's quantum networking vision and concrete pieces: the Quantum Network Entanglement Chip and a Network-Aware Quantum Compiler, plus how quantum capabilities augment classical systems today and the IBM partnership (from abstract only).
  • How: Entanglement distribution hardware plus a compiler that maps quantum programs onto network topology — the beginning of a distributed-quantum-systems networking stack.
  • Where applicable: Early research/vendor-vision stage; treat as strategic sensing, not deployable technology.

quantum-networking

items.title: AI Gave Every Attacker a Kubernetes Playbook. Isovalent Takes It Away - PSOSEC-2345
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Adjacent pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Duffie Cooley (Cisco)

  • Why: A PSO product pitch, but the underlying pattern — identity-aware (not IP-aware) network policy in K8s — is core to where this PM's cloud-native-security interests are heading.
  • What: Demonstration of replacing IP-based K8s network policy with identity-aware enforcement via Cilium, plus process-level visibility and nano-segmentation via Isovalent Runtime Security, integrated with Splunk ES for ATT&CK-mapped detections (from abstract only).
  • How: eBPF-based enforcement keyed to workload identity rather than IP/pod-label matching, catching east-west traffic that IP policies miss in ephemeral environments.
  • Where applicable: Cilium/Isovalent-specific; the identity-based-policy concept generalizes, but the specific enforcement is tied to this stack.

kubernetes network-security

items.title: Beyond the (Switch)-Port: Exploring the World of Host Networking - BRKNWT-2620
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Bruce McDougall (Cisco), Chris Lapp (Cisco)

  • Why: Host-side networking is where this PM's physical and cloud-native interests converge — kernel bypass, eBPF datapaths, CNI performance, and SmartNICs in one arc.
  • What: A tour from the ToR switch port down into the host: native OS packet paths, hypervisor networking, the Kubernetes CNI ecosystem, and emerging sub-100µs host-networking techniques (from abstract only).
  • How: Compares virtio/SR-IOV and vSwitch options (OVS, VPP), benchmarks CNI choices — Calico "just routes," Cilium's eBPF policy datapaths, VPP-backed CNIs for terabit throughput — and looks ahead at XDP/AF_XDP kernel bypass, eBPF congestion control, and SmartNICs fusing packet processing with AI inference.
  • Where applicable: Broadly applicable to Linux host networking and K8s; the real-world benchmark claims (terabit VPP CNIs, sub-100µs paths) should be probed for environment specifics.

linux-networking ebpf dpu

items.title: Building AI/ML Fabrics at Hyperscale: Architecture Evolutions, Challenges, Open Standards, Performance Characterization and Validation on Cisco SiliconOne-based Platforms. - BRKMSI-2014
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Masiuddin Mohammed (Cisco), Evan Knipp (Cisco)

  • Why: The single densest architectural map of where AI-scale DC fabrics are going — cluster size, topology generations, and DCI constraints are exactly the design questions a physical-networking PM needs answered.
  • What: A trace of AI fabric evolution from 4K/16K-GPU leaf-spine, to 64K-GPU Disaggregated Scheduled Fabric (DSF) two-tier with super-spines, to >200K-GPU three-tier scale-out, plus multi-DC DCI interconnect; paired with a benchmarking methodology for validating these fabrics (from abstract only).
  • How: Addresses scale-out concerns (fat flows, ECMP polarization, asymmetric failures, fault resilience) separately from scale-up concerns (~8x per-accelerator bandwidth for tensor-parallel, e.g. NVL72), and DCI demands of high-speed buffering and encryption over ~100 km / 1 ms RTT. Validation is done in production-like environments using open, standards-aligned test practices to minimize test drift.
  • Where applicable: Cisco-specific (Silicon One platforms) and hyperscaler-derived, but the topology taxonomy, failure-mode catalog, and benchmark methodology generalize to any large AI fabric build.

ai-networks data-center-fabric silicon

items.title: Cisco Nexus 9000 Architecture - BRKDCN-3939
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Faraz Taifehesmatian (Cisco)

  • Why: Switching silicon and forwarding mechanics are core to this PM; this is the internals session for Cisco's workhorse DC switch line.
  • What: An in-depth architecture study of the latest-generation Nexus 9000 modular and top-of-rack switches — ASIC architecture, forwarding mechanics, and physical design (from abstract only).
  • How: Walks the packet path through the ASIC and the hardware-enabled features that produce high-performance DC network services.
  • Where applicable: Nexus 9000-specific; useful as a concrete datapoint on merchant/custom silicon trade-offs and what a modern DC ASIC feature set looks like.

switching silicon

items.title: Control your destiny in the token-based AI economy with pluggable optics innovations - PSOMSI-1005
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Adjacent pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Ray Nering (Cisco), Yoav Schreiber (Cisco)

  • Why: Down-ranked as a PSO product session, but it carries the substantive technology story behind Cisco's optics roadmap: silicon photonics, 1.6T pluggables, and Linear Pluggable Optics.
  • What: How Cisco's 1.6T pluggable optics and Silicon Photonics serve AI back-end/front-end networks, and how LPO moves the DSP power draw from the module into the switch silicon (from abstract only).
  • How: Details the power-efficiency mechanics of LPO on Silicon One G300 platforms (liquid- and air-cooled) and Cisco's field-reliability approach: qualification, test, and over-the-wire firmware updates across deployed optics fleets.
  • Where applicable: Cisco-optics-specific; the LPO power trade-off (and its reach/reliability constraints) is an industry-wide decision point for anyone building 1.6T back-ends.

optics silicon

items.title: Designing RoCEv2 Networks for Distributed AI Training with Cisco Nexus 9000 - BRKDCN-2688
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Praveen Poojary (Cisco)

  • Why: Lossless/low-loss RDMA fabric tuning is the hardest operational problem in AI clusters today; this is the session that actually walks the PFC/ECN/congestion-control knobs.
  • What: A design-and-operate guide for RoCE fabrics purpose-built for training jobs of thousands to tens of thousands of GPUs running days-to-weeks, targeting near-lossless behavior and predictable AllReduce/AllGather throughput (from abstract only).
  • How: Covers the frontend/backend network separation common at hyperscalers and its implications for leaf-spine topology, routing, and failure domains; then congestion control, PFC/ECN, and QoS tuning for bursty, low-entropy AI flows.
  • Where applicable: Nexus 9000-specific in tooling, but the lossless-fabric design principles (entropy, incast, ECN thresholds) apply to any RoCEv2 backend fabric.

rdma congestion-control ai-networks

items.title: Failure Patterns in Modern Distributed Systems: Lessons from Major Internet Outages - BRKOPS-2000
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Wildcard pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Mike Hicks (Cisco)

  • Why: Outside the core interests, but a 90-minute analysis of real major outages (cloud providers, collaboration platforms, CDNs) with repeatable forensic patterns is high-value for anyone designing resilient distributed infrastructure.
  • What: Three failure patterns distilled from major incidents: coordination features becoming failure-distribution mechanisms, systems that look healthy while core functions silently break, and config changes cascading across interconnected systems (from abstract only).
  • How: Case-study walkthroughs using the ThousandEyes MCP server and its analytical framework to surface, interrogate, and codify patterns from real incident data — turning raw telemetry into repeatable forensic methodology. Led by the Principal Analyst behind The Internet Report.
  • Where applicable: Pattern-level and broadly applicable; the MCP-server-driven analysis is itself an early example of AI-tooling-assisted incident forensics.

troubleshooting sre

items.title: Hijacking Trust: Weaponizing Stolen Cookies and Tokens - BRKSEC-2132
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Stefan Duernberger (Cisco)

  • Why: Session/token theft is the dominant real-world auth attack vector, and this session covers the modern defensive stack — passkeys, token binding, shared signals — directly on this PM's identity interests.
  • What: How stolen cookies and tokens are weaponized, and the countermeasures: passkeys (FIDO/WebAuthn), OAuth 2.0 and OIDC flows, Google's Device-Bound Session Credentials (DBSC), Cisco Duo Passport, and the Shared Signals and Events (SSE) framework (from abstract only).
  • How: Walks implementation of each mechanism and how they combine in a Zero Trust architecture to kill replayable bearer credentials.
  • Where applicable: Standards-based and broadly applicable (DBSC is a browser standard-in-progress, SSE is OpenID Foundation work); the Duo Passport portion is product-specific.

authentication identity

items.title: Hunting the Invisible Army: Visibility for AI Agents & Non-human Identities - BRKSEC-2067
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Tal Kronrod (Cisco)

  • Why: NHI explosion is the identity story of the cycle; traditional ITDR built for humans misses machine-speed, broad-permission identities.
  • What: A framework and product demonstration (Cisco Identity Intelligence) for unified visibility and threat detection/response across service accounts, workloads, and autonomous AI agents in cloud, on-prem, and SaaS (from abstract only).
  • How: Applies identity intelligence — correlating inherited permissions, credential usage, and behavior — to detect threats from NHIs that never trip human-focused anomaly detection.
  • Where applicable: The NHI problem is universal, but the demo is Cisco's Identity Intelligence product; the framework's portability to other ITDR tooling should be probed.

identity observability

items.title: Life of a Packet in Kubernetes: A Network Engineer's Guide - BRKCLD-3734
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Nico Vibert (Cisco)

  • Why: A datapath-internals walkthrough of Kubernetes networking using Isovalent Cilium — squarely on this PM's core cloud-native interests (eBPF, Gateway API, overlays, BGP).
  • What: A full trace of a packet through a Kubernetes cluster — across nodes, overlays, policy, and egress — using Cilium as the dataplane, with live demos (from abstract only).
  • How: Unpacks VXLAN/Geneve overlays, Gateway API, Egress Gateway, BGP routing, IPsec encryption, Direct Server Return, multi-cluster Cluster Mesh, plus performance features BIG TCP and topology-aware traffic engineering; observability via Hubble, Cilium CLI, and Wireshark.
  • Where applicable: Cilium/Isovalent-centric but the K8s networking constructs (Gateway API, CNI, multicluster) are vendor-neutral; advanced session, assumes routing/overlay/LB fluency.

kubernetes ebpf cni

items.title: Modern Multi-Homing in VXLAN EVPN: Enabling vPC and ESI+ in Today's Data Centers - BRKDCN-2940
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Parth Patel (Cisco)

  • Why: EVPN ESI multihoming landing in NX-OS 10.6.1 is a real control-plane shift for Cisco fabrics; the vPC-vs-ESI trade-off is a live design decision.
  • What: A comparison of classic vPC and the new EVPN ESI multihoming (ESI+), covering how each works, what changes with ESI+, and when to choose one over the other (from abstract only).
  • How: Real design examples and packet-flow comparisons, framed around fabric scale, resiliency requirements, and operational model. Assumes prior vPC-VTEP knowledge.
  • Where applicable: NX-OS fabrics specifically; the ESI-MH model itself is the IETF standard mechanism also used by other vendors and SONiC, so the concepts travel well.

bgp data-center-fabric

items.title: Pig-in-the-Middle - TLS Decryption and Encrypted Visibility Engine Deep Dive on Cisco Secure Firewall - BRKSEC-3320
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Carol Trincia Dsouza (Cisco)

  • Why: Encrypted Client Hello plus post-quantum crypto is about to break passive TLS interception — a network-security sea change this PM needs to plan for.
  • What: A deep dive on the modern encryption stack as seen from the firewall: ECH, domain fronting, evasive VPNs, fake TLS, QUIC decryption, and how the Encrypted Visibility Engine fingerprints the source process of an encrypted connection without decrypting anything (from abstract only).
  • How: Live demos of decryption configuration (TLS and QUIC) and of encrypted-traffic analysis, including how a free CDN account can stack QUIC + ECH + encrypted DNS + post-quantum crypto into an opaque connection, and what that means for decryption policy.
  • Where applicable: Cisco Secure Firewall product context, but the threat/visibility analysis (ECH, PQ, QUIC obfuscation) is broadly relevant to any TLS-inspecting security stack.

tls firewall encryption

items.title: Real World Deployments: Architectural lessons learnt from a 100+ Node AI Factory Deployment - BRKXAR-2039
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Dave Lucas (Cisco), Nandu Shankar (Cisco)

  • Why: The closest thing in this program to an end-user case study with failure discussion — a real integration bring-up, not a clean-room reference architecture.
  • What: Lessons from standing up a 100+ node "AI factory" spanning compute, network, and storage, with dual GPU vendors, virtual and containerized workloads, RDMA-accelerated storage with GPUDirect, multi-tenant security, and a scalable RoCE front and back-end fabric (from abstract only).
  • How: Explicitly covers the failure modes that don't appear in config guides: multi-OS GPU driver inconsistencies, RoCE fabric optimization, cross-vendor GPU networking quirks, shared-services dependencies, cabling/topology missteps, and typical bottlenecks.
  • Where applicable: Deployment-specific (one environment, Cisco-built), but the cross-vendor integration pitfalls are broadly instructive for anyone running mixed-GPU AI infrastructure.

ai-networks troubleshooting

items.title: Reclaiming Your Agency: MCP, OAuth 2.1 and the Power to Automate Anything - BRKSEC-2065
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Jeremiah Williams (Cisco)

  • Why: Agentic identity is an emerging core interest, and this is the standards-level session — MCP authorization, OAuth 2.1, fine-grained authorization — rather than a product pitch.
  • What: How the emerging agentic-AI security stack works: Model Context Protocol (MCP), OAuth 2.1, fine-grained authorization, and related mechanisms for controlling what autonomous agents can access and do (from abstract only).
  • How: Explores how these standards combine to give agents delegated, scoped, auditable access to business applications — and notes the same machinery applies to human identity.
  • Where applicable: Standards-track and vendor-neutral (MCP, OAuth 2.1, fine-grained authz are IETF/OpenAI-ecosystem work); product agnosticism should be verified in the deck.

authorization identity api

items.title: Safeguarding the Internet's Backbone: Unleashing the Power of RPKI for Unbreakable IPv4 and IPv6 BGP Security - BRKENT-2179
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Jeffry Handal (Cisco), John Shea (Cisco)

  • Why: RPKI deployment is the practical, deployable answer to BGP hijacking — core internet-routing security with direct DC/WAN interconnect relevance.
  • What: Real-world BGP hijack incidents (criminal and nation-state) analyzed against what RPKI and related BGP capabilities would have prevented, plus deployment strategies and working configuration examples to start an RPKI rollout (from abstract only).
  • How: Route Origin Validation mechanics, deployment patterns (full vs partial ROV), and complementary BGP security capabilities.
  • Where applicable: Any organization operating BGP and announcing prefixes — vendor tooling is Cisco IOS-XR/IOS-XE but RPKI/RFC 6811 is standards-based and cross-vendor.

bgp network-security pki

items.title: Silicon One Unveiled: Diving into the power of Cisco silicon - BRKNWT-2624
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Ramesh Sivakolundu (Cisco), Dave Zacks (Cisco)

  • Why: Silicon One is the unifying silicon across Cisco's enterprise, SP, and AI portfolios; understanding its design rationale is directly relevant to physical DC networking decisions.
  • What: A deep-dive into how Silicon One is architected and why — the design choices, distinguishing features, and how its capabilities map to different network roles. Caveat: the abstract is noticeably hype-toned ("fast-paced... you will be glad you did!") and carries no specific technical claims, so depth must be verified in the room or on the recording (from abstract only).
  • How: Presented as silicon design-and-engineering rationale — not just feature lists but the why behind implementation choices, and how those translate into deployable designs.
  • Where applicable: Cisco silicon-specific; valuable mainly as the architectural underpinning for the AI-fabric and routing sessions above.

silicon

items.title: The Network Capability AI Has Been Waiting For - BRKPAR-1026
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Wildcard pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Nikhil Handigol (Forward)

  • Why: A partner session, but it points at a genuinely novel operational pattern: a mathematically accurate network digital twin as the reasoning layer for both human changes and autonomous AI agents.
  • What: Demonstration of pre-deployment verification of routing and firewall changes on a formal network model, catching regressions before production, and automated end-to-end impact assessment replacing manual approval cycles (from abstract only).
  • How: Formal verification of network state and behavior (the Forward Networks model-checking lineage) applied as the guardrail that lets AI agents act on production networks with verified-before-risk confidence.
  • Where applicable: Formal-model based, vendor- and device-neutral in principle (Forward ingests multi-vendor configs); the AI-agent-trust framing is early but directly relevant to where network automation is heading.

ml-for-networking testing

items.title: The New, QUIC Based Encrypted Protocol Stack Taking over the Internet and How to Deal with It - BRKSPM-2024
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Adjacent pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Andreas Enotiadis (Cisco), Bart Van de Velde (Cisco)

  • Why: Adjacent rather than core because of its service-provider framing, but the QUIC/HTTP-3/DoH/ECH stack it describes is the same visibility threat covered in BRKSEC-3320, with protocol-internals depth.
  • What: How the QUIC-based stack (QUIC + HTTP/3 + DoH + eSNI/ECH) is constructed and evolving — already claimed at ~50% of traffic and doubling every 18 months — and why it obsoletes the assumptions SP networks are built on: encryption kills application visibility, and congestion management moves into the application (from abstract only).
  • How: Analysis of the stack's visibility and flow-control behavior plus SP-side countermeasures for traffic visibility, QoE monitoring, and efficient use of scarce resources like 5G spectrum.
  • Where applicable: SP networks primarily; the protocol analysis applies to any operator of middleboxes and QoS infrastructure facing QUIC traffic.

http tls encryption

items.title: Troubleshooting SONIC on Cisco 8000: Learn how to Troubleshoot BGP, ACL, VxLAN on SONIC - TACMSI-2001
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

VASU Thatipalli (Cisco)

  • Why: SONiC is where open-source NOS development is actually happening; a TAC-lead troubleshooting session is a good signal of how production-mature SONiC on Cisco silicon has become.
  • What: Operational and control-plane debugging of BGP, ACLs, and VXLAN in SONiC environments, plus a structured troubleshooting framework covering data plane, control plane, and root-cause analysis (from abstract only).
  • How: SONiC CLI techniques and log analysis to isolate faults in production-scale deployments.
  • Where applicable: Cisco 8000 + SONiC deployments; the framework and CLI methods apply to SONiC generally, and the session doubles as a maturity readout for disaggregated switching.

open-source troubleshooting bgp

items.title: Unifying Kubernetes and the Data Center: Isovalent Private Networks over EVPN/VXLAN - BRKDCN-3668
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Marcos Hernández (Cisco)

  • Why: Bridges this PM's two worlds — K8s networking and DC EVPN fabric — with concrete control-plane and datapath mechanisms rather than hand-waving about "integration."
  • What: A blueprint for integrating Isovalent Private Networks (Cilium-based K8s) with external EVPN/VXLAN fabrics, including underlay/overlay connectivity, BGP control-plane setup, EVPN route-type advertisements, VRF instantiation, and VTEP configuration on both sides (from abstract only).
  • How: Details the specific route advertisements and datapath programming needed to stretch logical L2/L3 networks between Kubernetes and the Cisco fabric, and how the result supports distributed AI/ML application designs.
  • Where applicable: Isovalent + Cisco NX-OS/ACI-style fabrics specifically; the EVPN-into-K8s pattern is generalizable to any CNI that can speak BGP/EVPN.

kubernetes data-center-fabric

items.title: VXLAN EVPN: A Deep Dive into Packet Forwarding - BRKDCN-3966
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Lukas Krattiger (Cisco)

  • Why: EVPN/VXLAN datapath internals are a core interest — this is the "follow the packet" internals session, not a feature overview.
  • What: A day-in-the-life walkthrough of a VXLAN EVPN packet: routing and bridging behavior, and multi-destination (BUM) traffic handling, from ingress VTEP to egress VTEP and beyond (from abstract only).
  • How: Step-by-step datapath trace of encap/decap, ARP suppression, and multicast replication mechanics on the fabric.
  • Where applicable: Any VXLAN EVPN fabric; mechanism-focused rather than product-specific.

bgp data-center-fabric

items.title: Your AI Agents Don't Talk to My AI Agents - Let's Fix That! - BRKETI-1009
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Core pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Sabitha Krishnamurthy (Cisco)

  • Why: AGNTCY is a Linux Foundation open-source project defining agent interoperability infrastructure including agent identity — the federation/identity layer this PM tracks (analogous to SPIFFE's role for workloads).
  • What: An introduction to the Internet of Agents and AGNTCY.org's four core technologies: agent directory, agent identity, SLIM messaging, and observability — the shared substrate for cross-environment agent discovery, trust, and communication (from abstract only).
  • How: Technical overview plus practical multi-agent use cases demonstrated with shared code.
  • Where applicable: Open-source (Linux Foundation) and cross-vendor by design; early-stage, so expect evolving specs rather than settled interfaces.

identity standardization

items.title: Zero Trust for Agents - PSOSEC-2344
items.text:
Cisco Live US 2026 (Las Vegas) digest Program Adjacent pick Las Vegas · 31 May – 4 June 2026

Abstract

Tsailing Merrem (Cisco), Prabhu Barathi (Cisco)

  • Why: Down-ranked from core: this is product-positioning for Cisco's Zero Trust portfolio applied to agents, and the more substantive agentic-identity coverage is in BRKSEC-2065 and BRKSEC-2067.
  • What: The argument that autonomous agents become the "ultimate insider" without fine-grained authorization, and how Cisco is extending its Zero Trust access architecture to enforce scope, access control, and data security for an agentic workforce (from abstract only).
  • How: Extends existing Zero Trust enforcement points (identity-aware proxy/access) to agent identities and their permitted actions rather than just access.
  • Where applicable: Cisco Zero Trust portfolio-specific; useful mainly as a readout of how a major vendor plans to operationalize agent authorization.

zero-trust identity
